1  ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION AND AWARD COMPENSATION  CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT BY MODIFYING JUDGMENT AND  AWARD DATED 28.04.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO.516/2019 ON  THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND  MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL-VI, JAMKHANDI, IN THE  INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.
 -2-  NC: 2026:KHC-D:3648  MFA No. 101854 of 2021 HC-KAR

THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI)
1.

The claimant being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal vide Judgment dated 28.04.2021 passed in MVC No.516/2019 by the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VI, Jamkhandi, has preferred this appeal.

2. Brief facts, leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
On 05.06.2019, the claimant was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-48/Q-7889 towards Hunshikatti from Sangapur on the extreme left side of the Jamkhandi- Vijayapur road, near Hanuman Temple.
At that time, a Maruthi Desire VDI car bearing registration No.KA-48/Q- 9622 came from the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident dashing the motorcycle.
As a result, the claimant fell down and NC: 2026:KHC-D:3648 HC-KAR sustained grievous injuries and suffered permanent disability.

3. Thereafter, the claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, "M.V. Act") seeking compensation on account of the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
4. The owner-respondent No.1 filed a statement of objections contending that he is the owner of the vehicle and that the vehicle was insured with insurance company- respondent No.2.
It was further contended that the driver of the car possessed a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of the accident and the insurance policy was in force.
Hence, he prayed to dismiss the claim petition against respondent No.1-the owner.
Sri. Sukanand S/O Yankappa Shindoor vs Sri. Sadashiv S/O Shivalingappa ...

on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39975258/
2 5.
Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company filed its statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition.

It contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence NC: 2026:KHC-D:3648 HC-KAR as of the date of the accident and that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
Hence, it prayed to dismiss the claim petition against the Insurance Company.
6. The Tribunal, based on the pleadings of the parties, framed the relevant issues.

7. To substantiate his case, the claimant examined himself as PW-1, examined the panch as PW-2 and marked 11 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
8.
In rebuttal, the respondents before the tribunal did not lead any oral evidence but got marked three documents as Ex.R1 to Ex.R3 with consent.

9. The Tribunal, after assessing the oral and documentary evidence on record, partly allowed the claim petition with costs vide judgment dated 28.04.2021 and awarded a compensation of Rs.3,41,098/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realization, and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3648 HC-KAR 10.
Being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed the present appeal.
11. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
12. The learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
He further submitted that since the accident is of 2019, the Tribunal ought to have taken the notional income at Rs.13,250/- as per the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
However, the Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.11,000/- which is on the lower side.
Hence, on this ground, he prayed to allow the appeal and enhance the compensation.

13. Per contra, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal itself is on the higher side, and that there are no NC: 2026:KHC-D:3648 HC-KAR grounds to enhance the compensation.
Hence, he prays to dismiss the appeal.

14. Perused the records and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
15.
The point, that would arise for the consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.
16. It is an undisputed fact that the claimant met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries.

In order to prove the occurrence of the accident, the claimant has produced the charge sheet marked Sri. Sukanand S/O Yankappa Shindoor vs Sri. Sadashiv S/O Shivalingappa ... on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39975258/
3 as Ex.P7.
17.
The Tribunal, considering Ex.P7, has rightly held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

Regarding quantum of compensation:
18.

It is the case of the claimant that he was working doing agriculture and earning Rs.3,00,000/-
per annum, and that he was aged about 35 years as of the date of the accident.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3648 HC-KAR 19.
To prove his income, the claimant has not produced any documentary proof.
In the absence of income proof, the notional income has to be taken as Rs.13,250/- per month as per the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for 2019.

20. The claimant has examined the doctor as PW-2, who has deposed that he examined the claimant and issued the disability certificate marked as Ex.P10, stating that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 18% to the right lower limb.
However, the Tribunal has taken the disability at 8%, which appears to be just and proper.
From the records, it is clear that the claimant was aged about 37 years as of the date of the accident.

21. In view of the above discussion, the compensation is reassessed under the following heads:
Compensation amount Particulars in (Rs.) Pain and suffering 60,000/-
Conveyance attendance charges 15,000/-
 food and nourishment  NC: 2026:KHC-D:3648 HC-KAR

Medical Expenses 69,698/-
 Loss of income during laid up  39,750/-
 period (13,250 x 3)
 Loss of amenities  40,000/-
 Loss of future income (13,250 Sri. Sukanand S/O Yankappa Shindoor vs Sri. Sadashiv S/O Shivalingappa ... on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39975258/
4  1,90,800/-
 x12 x 15 x 8%)
 Total 4,15,248/-
 Compensation awarded by the  3,41,098/-
 Tribunal  Reduced compensation 74,150/-
 22.
Thus claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.74,150/-, which is rounded off to Rs.75,000/-.

For the foregoing,
the point is answered accordingly,
23.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
(i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and the award  dated 28.04.2021 passed in MVC No.516/2019 by the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VI, Jamkhandi,
is hereby modified.

NC: 2026:KHC-D:3648 HC-KAR (iii) The claimant entitled to a total compensation of Rs.4,15,248/- as against Rs.3,41,098/- awarded by the Tribunal, with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petition till realization of the amount.
The compensation is enhanced by Rs.75,000/-.
(iv) The Insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest within 8 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
(v) The Tribunal records, and the amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal concerned, forthwith.
